title: Lights Out at Marrowby
pitch: The sun hasn't risen for nineteen days. Tonight the last train to the coast is due through a moorland junction whose signal lamp is the only light for forty miles.
premise: Nineteen days ago the sun failed to come up, and on the third day the stars went out too. Since then Marrowby Junction, a signal box, a platform, a waiting room and a lamp room on a high moor, has kept one lamp burning on its signal post, because the radio said the last train to Saltcoats would run when the line was clear, and somebody has to clear it. You are the people who ended up there: the signalwoman who never left her post, and the ones who walked toward her light across the moor. The paraffin is nearly gone. Something has started humming in the rails.
setting: Marrowby Junction, a railway halt on a high moor in the north of England, nineteen days into the dark

posting.header: MISSING: THE 6:10 TO SALTCOATS. LAST SEEN AT MARROWBY
posting.reward: A seat on the last train, if it comes

gmNotes:
This is a Ten Candles module, not a cast to survive: everyone dies, and the night is about how. The pre-made concepts are optional; players write their own traits, moments and brinks at the table either way.

Pace it by the light. Early scenes are about keeping the lamp lit and deciding who to trust. Middle scenes are about the paraffin running out and what people will burn instead. The end is the tunnel, because the coast line runs through it and the hum comes out of it.

The train is real. It's coming. It doesn't stop. Whether it carries anyone away is up to the last scene, and it should cost the most.

Never give Them a weakness but light. Don't name Them. Let the table's truths decide what They wear.

letters.title: The last entry in the train register
letters.when: When the paraffin runs low (about five candles)
letters.text: You find it in your own handwriting, in the train register, dated the second night: "6:10 Saltcoats passed Marrowby, 2 min late, all lamps lit, no one at the windows." You don't remember writing it. You don't remember the train. The next line is in your hand too, and the ink is still wet: "Line clear."

acts.title: Keep the Lamp Lit
acts.subtitle: Nineteen days dark. Strangers round a stove, and paraffin for three nights at most.

acts.title: What Will Burn
acts.subtitle: Light is the only currency left on the moor. Spend it.

acts.title: The Line Is Clear
acts.subtitle: The block bell rings the long code. Something is coming up from the coast.

acts.title: Through the Tunnel
acts.subtitle: Gallows Hill. A mile and a quarter of dark, and one candle burning in the middle.

acts.title: The Last Light
acts.subtitle: One candle left. The train does not slow down.

rumors.text: Ida chalks the paraffin level on the lamp-room wall every night, and the marks are getting closer together.
Somebody keeps a candle lit in the refuge halfway through Gallows Hill tunnel. Nobody at the junction will say who.
The cars at the crossing still have batteries under the bonnet. Two hundred yards of dark there, and two hundred back.
The stationmaster came back out of the tunnel on the seventh night, they say. His wife lets him in at the back door.
The 6:10 to Saltcoats went through on the second night, packed to the doors and every lamp lit.
The postwoman's got a letter in that sack for every one of us, and she's read them all.
The army's running a relief train up from the coast with searchlights. It'll stop for anyone who waves a lamp.
A man on the road swore the sun still comes up over Saltcoats. It's only dark up here on the moor.

notices.title: MISSING: The Stationmaster
notices.text: Went into Gallows Hill tunnel on the fifth day to look for the train. Cap and long coat. If you hear him on the line, do not answer.

notices.title: Curfew: Stay Inside the Light
notices.text: By order of the signalwoman: no one leaves the lamplight once the stove is banked. No one opens the waiting-room door to a knock. No exceptions.

notices.title: Last Seen: The Edge of the Light
notices.text: A figure in a coat like the one missing from the hook, standing just past the lamplight, facing in. It did not answer to its name.

notices.title: Reward: A Seat on the Last Train
notices.text: Promised to whoever fetches the batteries from the crossing and carries them back into the light. There are fewer seats than there were this morning.

notices.title: Lamp Room: Dry
notices.text: Last drum of paraffin emptied and chalked off. The lamp room is closed. What still burns is all there is.

sources: Original module for Ten Candles (Cavalry Games). You need the game to play: this is a play aid, and every rule here is our own summary.

module.intro:
It has been dark for nineteen days. Not night: dark. The sun didn't rise, and three days later the stars went out one by one, like lamps along a street. Phones died. The radio still talks sometimes, a man reading the same list of railway stations, and at the end of the list he says the last train to the coast will run when the line is clear.

Marrowby Junction is a signal box, a platform and a stone waiting room on the high moor, forty miles from anywhere with a name. On the signal post a single paraffin lamp is burning. You can see it from miles away, the only light in the world. Every one of you walked toward it. Some of you walked a long way.

The stove in the waiting room is warm. There is tea, of a kind. Ida Kell, who has worked this box for thirty years, has kept the lamp lit every hour of every day, and tonight, for the first time, she has said out loud how much paraffin is left.

In the rails, very faintly, something has started to hum.
module.goal: Keep the signal lit until the last train comes through, and get someone, anyone, aboard it.
module.them: They come up the line from Gallows Hill tunnel. You hear Them before anything else: a hum in the rails like a train that never arrives, then the smell of wet coal. Near the light They are only a pressure at the edge of it, a crowd that keeps its distance. In the dark They are close enough to touch. People who go out to Them come back to the edge of the lamplight and stand there, facing in, and do not answer to their names. Let the table decide what else They are. Light is the only thing They won't cross.

areas.name: The signal box
areas.text: A wooden box on stilts with a long frame of levers and a brass block bell that still rings when the line ahead is occupied. Ida sleeps in the chair. The windows look down the line both ways: north to the moor, south to the tunnel mouth.
finds: a hand lamp with a red glass

areas.name: The waiting room
areas.text: Stone walls, a pot-bellied stove, two benches, a timetable under glass with the 6:10 circled in pencil by someone who has stopped coming in. People have left things here: shoes, a pram with nothing in it, a stack of letters addressed to the same house.

areas.name: The lamp room
areas.text: A lean-to that smells of paraffin and burnt wick. Racks of station lamps, most of them dry. One drum of paraffin with a dipstick: Ida marks the level in chalk on the wall each night, and the marks are getting closer together.
finds: a box of tinned candles from the war

areas.name: The level crossing
areas.text: Where the moor road crosses the line, two hundred yards north. The gates are shut. Cars stand on the road behind them, doors open, lights long dead. Footprints in the frost lead from the cars toward the lamp and stop halfway.
finds: a child's torch with one weak bulb

areas.name: The stationmaster's house
areas.text: A cottage below the platform. The stationmaster went into the tunnel on the fifth day to look for the train and didn't come back. His wife still sets two places at the table. She won't come up to the light. She says she can hear him on the line.
finds: a family Bible with names crossed out in pencil

areas.name: Gallows Hill tunnel
areas.text: A mile and a quarter of brick-lined dark under the hill, the only way the coast line goes. The hum comes from inside. Water runs down the walls. Halfway along there's a refuge alcove where someone has left a lit candle, and nobody knows who keeps lighting it.
finds: a lit candle in the refuge

stages.title: Keep the lamp lit
stages.text: Strangers sizing each other up in the waiting room. Who walked in from where, and what did they see on the way? Ida says there's paraffin for three nights at most. Someone suggests going down to the stationmaster's house for supplies.
beats: the block bell rings once with nothing on the line
a figure stands at the edge of the light and won't come closer
the radio reads the list of stations and leaves Marrowby out

stages.title: What will burn
stages.text: The paraffin is going. Light becomes the only currency. People start burning things to keep it: letters, benches, the timetable, the pram. The cars at the crossing have batteries. Someone has to cross two hundred yards of dark to get them.
beats: the stationmaster's wife calls from the dark by name
a lamp goes out in the lamp room though no one touched it
Ida writes in the register and won't say what

stages.title: The line is clear
stages.text: The bell rings properly now, the long code for a train approaching. It's coming from the coast end, through the tunnel. For it to take anyone, someone has to set the signal and someone has to be on the platform, and both need light.
beats: the hum becomes a rhythm, like wheels
someone who went out comes back to the edge of the light, facing in
the last full lamp has to go one way or the other: the signal or the platform

stages.title: Through the tunnel
stages.text: The train hasn't come out of Gallows Hill. Whatever's holding it is in there. The only light left is what you can carry. The candle in the refuge alcove is still burning.
beats: the trolley on the rails, pushed into the dark
the refuge candle, and whoever lit it
the far end of the tunnel, where there might be a grey light, or might not

module.lastStand: One candle. Let it be the lamp on the signal post, or the candle from the tunnel refuge. The train comes. It doesn't slow down. Its windows are lit, every one, and there's no one at them, and its light is the last light. Ask each player in turn what their character does as it passes.

suggestedTruths: The block bell rang twice tonight with nothing on the line.
Ida has marked the paraffin level lower than it really is.
There is a smell of wet coal in the waiting room that won't go away.
The man on the radio sounded closer tonight.
Someone's coat is missing from the hook by the stove.
The footprints at the crossing have moved a little nearer to the light.
The stationmaster's wife has laid a third place at her table.
The candle in the tunnel refuge is still burning.
